faq: Why not just install an existing plugin?
Sometimes you should, and we will say so. A custom extension makes sense when plugins cost more than the feature is worth, slow your store or do ten things when you need one.
Will it work with my theme and other plugins?
We test it with your active theme and key plugins on a staging copy. Because it uses standard WooCommerce hooks, it normally works alongside most themes and payment or shipping plugins.
Do I need to give you access to my live site?
No. We start from a staging copy. If you want us to install it live, add us as an administrator user for that day. We never ask for your passwords.
Can I reuse or sell the extension?
You own the code, so you can reuse it on your other stores. Selling it widely is possible too, and we can tidy it up for release if you want that as a separate piece of work.
desc:
A custom WooCommerce extension for one store is a small plugin that adds the exact feature your shop needs and nothing more. Ecom Swift LLC builds it as a lightweight plugin that you own, tested on a staging copy before it goes near your live store.

## What is a custom WooCommerce extension for one store?

It is a plugin written for a single shop and a single purpose. It is not published in a directory and it is not sold to anyone else. It might add a wholesale price rule, a delivery date picker, a custom order status, a product add-on field or a special checkout rule.

Because it only does one job, it stays small. There is no settings maze, no promotional banners and no code for features you will never use.

## When a custom extension beats an off-the-shelf plugin

Public plugins are built for thousands of stores, so they carry options that most shops never touch. That extra code still loads, still needs updates and still creates places for conflicts. When a plugin does ten things and you need one, the other nine are a cost.

A custom extension also fits your process exactly. If your wholesale buyers get a price rule based on their account type, or your bakery needs a pickup date that skips Sundays, a tailored rule matches the real work. Staff stop working around a tool that almost fits.

## How a focused extension helps your store run

The benefit is mostly operational. A custom order status can show your team which orders are waiting for artwork approval. A delivery date picker can cut the emails you send to ask when a customer wants an order. A role-based price rule can remove a manual discount step for every trade customer.

Each of these saves staff time and reduces mistakes. A smaller plugin also tends to be easier to keep compatible when WooCommerce and WordPress update.

## What a good custom extension includes

- One clearly defined feature agreed in writing before any code is written.
- Hooks and filters used the way WooCommerce documents them, rather than edits to theme or core files.
- Compatibility with your current theme and active plugins.
- A minimal settings screen, only where a setting is truly needed.
- Order data saved properly and shown in admin where your team needs it.
- Rules by product, category or user role, where the feature calls for them.
- Input sanitized and output escaped.
- A clean install, update and removal path.
- An installable plugin file that your developer can read and extend.

## What we do

First we confirm the feature in plain language, including edge cases such as what should happen for guests, for refunds or for products that do not qualify. Then we set up a staging copy of your store and build the extension there.

We test the feature with your theme, your shipping and payment plugins and sample orders. After your approval, we deliver the plugin file and install it on the live store, or give you instructions to do it yourself. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many features are included and whether you get an admin settings page, order exports, role-based rules and a handover call.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the problem you are solving, not only the feature you imagine.
- Give examples of real orders that should and should not trigger the rule.
- Decide who on your team will approve the finished feature.
- Take a full site backup on the day the extension goes live.
- Ask for an owner guide if more than one person will manage the extension.

**Avoid:**
- Asking for many unrelated features in one small plugin.
- Pasting snippets into a theme functions file, where updates can erase them.
- Changing the rules mid-build without agreeing the change first.
- Testing only on the live store.
- Assuming a feature will work with a plugin we have not been told about.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a wholesale seller who needs prices to change by customer role. It suits a local food business that needs delivery dates and custom order statuses. It also suits an owner whose store carries three heavy plugins to get one small behavior and who wants to replace them with a single tidy extension.

## What we need from you

Send a short written description of the feature, a few example orders and the theme and plugins you use. We never need your password. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or administrator user, or through a staging copy, and we reply with a checklist after your order. The finished plugin is yours to keep, install and modify.
